questions.q: Find the verb: 'Swimming in the morning keeps me healthy.'
questions.a: 'keeps' — 'swimming' is the subject here (an activity as a thing), not the verb. A wrong answer 'swimming' reveals the student labels any -ing word a verb without checking what drives the sentence.

questions.q: Which gear: 'She will visit her grandmother tomorrow.'
questions.a: Future — will + visit. A wrong answer 'present because visit looks plain' shows the student ignores the helper 'will' which IS the gear lever.

questions.q: Verb or not: 'The tired boy slept soundly.' — is 'tired' a verb here?
questions.a: No — 'tired' describes the boy (adjective); 'slept' is the verb. A wrong answer shows the student labels any past-form word a verb without checking its job in the sentence.

questions.q: Every ______ sentence needs at least one, and its form changes with time: 'She walks', 'She walked', 'She will walk' — same engine, three gears.
Fill in the blank: A verb is the ______ word — it names an action (run, eat, think) or a state (is, seem, have).
Fill in the blank: Find the ______: 'The bird flew over the tall tree slowly.' Which word can you act out? 'flew'.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student finds the verb(s) in any sentence, distinguishes action verbs from being-verbs, and identifies which gear (present/past/future) the sentence is in.
